Let \(q=2^{-1}\). Since all terms are nonnegative, we may interchange the sums:

\[
S=\sum_{m=1}^{100}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} q^{\lfloor 101k/m\rfloor}.
\]

For a fixed \(m\), write \(k=jm+r\) with \(j\ge 0\) and \(0\le r<m\). Then

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{101k}{m}\right\rfloor
=101j+\left\lfloor \frac{101r}{m}\right\rfloor.
\]

Thus

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} q^{\lfloor 101k/m\rfloor}
=
\frac{q^{101}+\sum_{r=1}^{m-1}q^{\lfloor 101r/m\rfloor}}{1-q^{101}}.
\]

So

\[
S=\frac{100q^{101}+A}{1-q^{101}},
\qquad
A=\sum_{1\le r<m\le 100}2^{-\lfloor 101r/m\rfloor}.
\]

Now compute \(A\). For fixed \(m\), let

\[
F_n=\left\lfloor \frac{nm}{101}\right\rfloor.
\]

For \(1\le n\le 99\), the number of \(r\) with \(1\le r<m\) and \(\lfloor 101r/m\rfloor=n\) is

\[
F_{n+1}-F_n.
\]

Hence

\[
A=\sum_{m=1}^{100}\sum_{n=1}^{99}(F_{n+1}-F_n)2^{-n}.
\]

For each fixed \(m\),

\[
\sum_{n=1}^{99}(F_{n+1}-F_n)2^{-n}
=
\sum_{n=1}^{99}F_n2^{-n}+F_{100}2^{-99},
\]

using \(F_1=0\) and \(2^{-(n-1)}-2^{-n}=2^{-n}\). Also

\[
F_{100}=\left\lfloor \frac{100m}{101}\right\rfloor=m-1.
\]

Therefore

\[
A=\sum_{n=1}^{99}2^{-n}\sum_{m=1}^{100}\left\lfloor \frac{nm}{101}\right\rfloor
+2^{-99}\sum_{m=1}^{100}(m-1).
\]

Since \(101\) is prime,

\[
\sum_{m=1}^{100}\left\lfloor \frac{nm}{101}\right\rfloor=50(n-1),
\]

and

\[
\sum_{m=1}^{100}(m-1)=4950.
\]

Thus

\[
A=50\sum_{n=1}^{99}(n-1)2^{-n}+4950\cdot 2^{-99}.
\]

Now

\[
\sum_{n=1}^{99}(n-1)2^{-n}=1-100\cdot 2^{-99},
\]

so

\[
A=50(1-100\cdot 2^{-99})+4950\cdot 2^{-99}
=50(1-2^{-99}).
\]

Finally,

\[
S=\frac{100\cdot 2^{-101}+50(1-2^{-99})}{1-2^{-101}}
=\frac{50(1-2^{-100})}{1-2^{-101}}
=\frac{100(2^{100}-1)}{2^{101}-1}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{100(2^{100}-1)}{2^{101}-1}}
\]
